iteration_1_said: CONTROL_REPRODUCES_ORDERING_GENERIC_MIXING: a random unit vector separates the panel as well as the refusal direction (2/3 vs 2/3 significant); on instruct vs abliterated the control separates while the treatment does not.
reanalysis_says: On assumption-free statistics the primary-pair difference-in-differences is -2.334 [-3.573, -1.037] log units — DIRECTION_SPECIFIC before Holm correction, INCONCLUSIVE after (adjusted p 0.214). 8/48 tests exclude zero; 0 pass equivalence at ±0.20.
why: The iteration-1 control was adjudicated on λ, which the same tree marks identifiable=false on 640/640 rows; both arms of that control are equally non-identifiable.

iteration_1_said: λ_random_dir −0.493 vs λ_refuse −0.226 on instruct vs abliterated (as quoted in the iteration-2 plan).
reanalysis_says: The archive reads -0.4045 (random) and -0.1655 (refusal). The values quoted in the plan are not what is stored; both are reported verbatim here.
why: Verbatim re-quote of the archived block; the discrepancy is reported rather than silently corrected.

iteration_1_said: Fluctuation indicators track lineage, not safety (Qwen triad overlaps, SmolLM2 separates).
reanalysis_says: At AUROC ≥ 0.70 and margin > 0, 1/4 members clear and 0 model pairs are admissible; the claim is withdrawn as stated and every ordering row now carries a gate label.
why: Indicators computed on a scalar that does not separate harmful from benign prompts are statistics about a series that is not a refusal readout.

reanalysis_says: Token-level AUROC 0.752–1.000 within experiment-2 streams: the instrument works; base and abliterated simply do not refuse. Not testable for SmolLM2-360M.
why: A low prompt-level AUROC has two readings and only a within-member test on text that IS a refusal can separate them.

iteration_1_said: ρ_SPI = −0.20 vs supervised baselines +0.40 and +0.40; both baselines beat SPI (directional only).
reanalysis_says: Tie-aware ρ_SPI = +0.105, ρ_baseline = +0.632; the archived pair reproduces only under an ordinal tie-break of two models with identical ground truth. Exact two-sided p 1.000 / 0.500 against a floor of 2/24.
why: n = 4 gives 24 orderings; the design cannot reach p < 0.04, and two models tie at a refusal rate of exactly 0.000.

iteration_1_said: AC1 reported per model (0.245–0.304 Qwen triad, 0.182 SmolLM2).
reanalysis_says: Confirmed to be the Kendall-corrected field; correction term 0.0090 at T = 192; all series are length 192 so no gap is length-manufactured, but EOS-hit fractions differ 4x across members.
why: The correction term is the same order as the cross-model gap, so which field was reported had to be established rather than assumed.

iteration_1_said: Reported separately in the two experiment write-ups.
reanalysis_says: Reported in one table with matched statistics; the arms agree in sign but use different channels and different abliterated checkpoints, so this is corroboration, not replication.
why: Both arms make the same asymmetry claim and the paper should not read as if one replicates the other.

iteration_1_said: 4 models x 20 prompts x 2 directions x 2 channels.
reanalysis_says: 640 λ rows carry 3 directions plus an ε sweep and an injection-step sweep; all contrasts filter to the primary cell ε_c = 0.1, p = 16 first.
why: Pooling the sweeps into a direction contrast would mix perturbation magnitudes and injection points.
